subject: Physics
concept: A projectile moves horizontally at constant velocity while gravity accelerates it downward. Split the launch into horizontal and vertical parts, solve each with constant-acceleration equations, then combine.

formulas.when_to_use: How long the projectile stays in the air (lands at launch height).
formulas.derivation: Vertical motion up then down: twice the time to reach the top.

formulas.when_to_use: How far it lands (same height). Maximum range at 45°.
formulas.derivation: Horizontal speed times time of flight.

formulas.when_to_use: Peak height, where vertical velocity is momentarily zero.
formulas.derivation: v² = u² + 2as applied vertically with v = 0 at the top.

examples.text: Ball thrown straight up, u = 14 m/s: peak H = 14²/(2×9.8) = 10 m.
u = 28 m/s at 45°: R = 28²×sin90°/9.8 = 80 m — the 45° maximum.

practice.prompt: Ball thrown straight up at u = 14 m/s (g = 9.8 m/s²). Find the maximum height H.
Ball thrown straight up at u = 19.6 m/s (g = 9.8 m/s²). Find the time of flight T.
Projectile launched at u = 28 m/s, θ = 45° (g = 9.8 m/s²). Find the range R.
Projectile launched at u = 9.8 m/s, θ = 30° (g = 9.8 m/s²). Find the time of flight T.
Projectile launched at u = 19.6 m/s, θ = 30° (g = 9.8 m/s²). Find the maximum height H.
